text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 10.6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #0e1f40
font-size: 7.4px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #334155

g.text: 1 Mouth — teeth cut and grind; saliva contains amylase

text.style: font-size: 7.4px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #334155

g.text: 2 Oesophagus — peristalsis pushes food to the stomach

text.style: font-size: 7.4px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #334155

g.text: 3 Stomach — hydrochloric acid and pepsin digest protein

text.style: font-size: 7.4px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #334155

g.text: 4 Duodenum — bile (from the liver) and pancreatic juice

text.style: font-size: 7.4px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #334155

g.text: 5 Ileum — villi absorb the digested food

text.style: font-size: 7.4px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #334155

g.text: 6 Caecum and appendix — little function in humans

text.style: font-size: 7.4px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #334155

g.text: 7 Colon — absorbs water and mineral salts 8 Rectum — stores faeces

text.style: font-size: 7.4px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #334155

g.text: 9 Liver (makes bile) 10 Gall bladder (stores bile) 11 Pancreas
